result.note: Tests the scheme name, the targeted component self-sufficiency levels, and the outlay and assembly-to-components shift.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, India approved 29 proposals for domestic manufacture of components such as PCBs, capacitors and rare-earth magnets. Under which scheme were these proposals approved?
options: Production Linked Incentive Scheme for IT Hardware
questions.explain: The package was approved under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme and covers PCBs, rare-earth magnets, capacitors, relays and EV inductors. To qualify for incentives, companies must also develop design and engineering capabilities in India.
questions.source: The INR 7,104 crore (USD 751 million) package under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme covers PCBs, rare-earth magnets, capacitors, relays, and EV inductors.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the electronics component manufacturing proposals approved by India in March 2026:
items: The approved package was worth INR 7,104 crore (USD 751 million).
Before this round, India's electronics manufacturing was concentrated in the assembly of finished products.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both statements are correct. The INR 7,104 crore package targets inputs such as PCBs and relays rather than finished-product assembly. Earlier schemes rewarded production volume, while this one ties subsidies to design and engineering capability built in India.
questions.source: Until now, India's electronics manufacturing has been concentrated in assembly of finished products.
